title: 2014 Virgin Galactic crash
summary: VSS Enterprise broke apart in flight during powered test flight four when co-pilot Michael Alsbury prematurely unlocked the feathering system at Mach 0.92. The NTSB determined that inadequate design safeguards, poor pilot training, and lack of FAA oversight allowed a single human error to destroy the aircraft.
probable_cause: The co-pilot's premature unlocking of the air brake feathering system during rocket-powered ascent at transonic speed caused the vehicle to break apart. Contributing factors were inadequate design safeguards that failed to prevent the hazard, insufficient pilot training, and inadequate FAA oversight of the experimental program.

factors.evidence: the feathering system was not protected against single-point human failure; the system could be unlocked at transonic speeds with no fail-safe mechanism (p. 3)
the NTSB cited poor pilot training and co-pilot's lack of rigorous training for the program (p. 3)
the co-pilot was described as potentially anxious without recent flight experience (p. 3)
lack of rigorous federal oversight by the FAA (p. 3)
the co-pilot prematurely unlocked the feathering system's lever at slightly above Mach 1 (p. 3)
the feathering system deployed and the space plane violently broke apart (p. 3)

events.text: VSS Enterprise released from WhiteKnightTwo carrier aircraft and rocket engine fires
Feathering system lock-unlock lever moved to unlocked position as aircraft reaches Mach 0.92 during rocket acceleration
SpaceShipTwo violently breaks apart at transonic speed creating 35-mile debris field
Co-pilot Michael Alsbury killed; pilot Peter Siebold seriously injured and transported to hospital
